chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Yusuf al-Bazzaz, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Indeed, among the people with the most intense regret on the Day of Judgment is the one who described [himself as] just, then acted contrary to it.
ai.seo_question: Who will have the most regret on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the severity of *taqarruf* (professing what one does not practice), particularly regarding justice (*adl*), a core tenet of faith. It warns that the dissonance between verbal affirmation and practical action leads to the most profound spiritual regret on the Day of Judgment, serving as a critique of superficial piety. This concept is often linked to the idea that true justice requires both internal conviction and external consistency in deeds.
